questions.question: What exactly should the manual fallback push? Today only two commits exist locally beyond the server tip H6 b4604bc: D-475 22b0a8c and R 71dfbbe. All the Lane A and Lane B work for this task (plans, reviews, r3 child, packets) is outside the repository under C:/CoWork/outputs, so it is not committed and cannot be pushed as is.

options.label: Hold; review r3 first (Recommended)
options.description: No push now. I do Lane A's exact-byte review of Lane B's r3 child, capture script and wrapper. The push stays at the end of the guarded cycle (publication → health record → Lane B review → your acceptance), as D-425 and the cycle release require.

options.label: Push D-475 and R only
options.description: Manual fallback outside the guarded cycle: fresh gates and two checks, then ls-remote must show b4604bc, one non-force push of 71dfbbe by full ID, ls-remote must show 71dfbbe, and a completion proof. The published graph would still lag D-475 (drift stays open). No external files are pushed.

options.label: Commit packets, then push
options.description: First transfer the selected external Lane A and Lane B records into the repository as new commits, then push. That is a transfer, which is currently held; it needs you to name the files, the destination folders and the commit plan first.

questions.question: Lane B's worklog also asks Lane A to review the exact bytes of r3 (child entry.r3.mjs 52ff2b33…, capture script, wrapper, manifest 8cde0d4e…). Should I do that review this turn?

options.label: Yes, review r3 now (Recommended)
options.description: Read-only exact-byte review against F-1, F-2 and F-4, written to a new external packet. No target, stand-in or fault case runs.

options.label: No, only the push decision
options.description: Leave the r3 review for a later turn.
